modal.settings.section.kdf_settings_intr: Unlock RAM lives in vault.header, not config.toml. Changing it verifies your password and rewrites vault.header plus the key wrap in contents/. The vault must be closed. Use Save in the footer after choosing a preset and entering the password.

modal.settings.field.security.mode_locke: Close this vault (or wait until it finishes opening or closing) before changing password memory. Recovery is OK.
modal.settings.field.security.mode_help: Controls only the vault unlock password. Default: keep it in RAM so lock does not ask again. Never save re-asks on lock as a presence check (it does not re-encrypt). Disk session files are less secure / insecure. Applies to encrypted directory and plain storage.
modal.settings.field.security.mode_help_: Controls only the vault unlock password for plaintext-on-disk vaults. Lock still uses the open session; Never save only confirms it is you before wiping the folder. Disk session files are more relevant here because files are readable on the volume while open.
modal.settings.field.close.require_unmou: Independent of idle auto-close. When enabled, the virtual mount is torn down if the OS suspends or hibernates.
modal.settings.field.seven_zip.encrypt_f: Recommended. Names are hidden inside the .7z until you enter the password.
If disabled, anyone can list file and folder names in the .7z without the password — only the file contents stay encrypted.
modal.settings.field.kdf.import_package: This .zip already has Upriv ciphertext inside. Unlock RAM is stored in the vault header and is not chosen again on import.
modal.settings.field.policy.external_edi: While this vault is open, files appear on a virtual mount. Choose whether only Upriv or also system apps may open them.
modal.settings.option.policy.external_ed: VS Code, your file manager, and other system apps cannot access the mount path.
Editors and file managers can open files through the mount.
modal.settings.field.policy.copy_outside: Whether drag-and-drop, Save As, or shell copy to Desktop, USB, or /tmp is blocked at the mount layer (independent of the setting above).
modal.settings.option.policy.copy_block_: Try to prevent copies to Desktop, removable drives, and temp folders while the vault is open.
modal.settings.option.policy.copy_allow_: Processes that can access the mount may leave plaintext outside the vault folder.
modal.settings.option.security.session_r: + Unlock once per session; lock does not ask again. − Password stays in RAM until you quit the app or lock the vault.
modal.settings.option.security.prompt_op: + Prompt on open and lock (presence check). − Password string is kept neither in RAM nor on disk. Session keys stay in RAM while open; lock does not wrap contents/ with a newly typed password.
modal.settings.option.security.disk_clos: + Lock without retyping after the first unlock. − Stores a session file on disk; opening still asks for the password.
modal.settings.option.security.disk_open: Disk session for open and close
+ Open and close without retyping. − Writes an encrypted session file to disk (not RAM); disk access may allow reuse to unlock.
modal.settings.option.storage.encrypted_: + Virtual folder (desktop) or in-app files (mobile); bytes on disk stay in contents/. Export a .zip of that ciphertext or a .7z when you need a file. − Needs a mount or in-app file manager while open.

modal.help.title: Help
modal.help.hint: Short guides for Upriv. Search filters sections in the current language.
modal.help.body.overview.1: Upriv manages encrypted vaults. At rest each vault is a contents/ folder (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305). You can copy that folder into an ordinary .zip (recommended) or export a portable .7z.
modal.help.body.overview.2: A vault is open (you edit files) or closed (encrypted on disk). The list shows the current state with a colored badge. Recovery appears if close did not finish cleanly.
modal.help.body.overview.3: By default, files stay encrypted on disk while the vault is open. On desktop you work through a virtual folder; on mobile, through the in-app file manager. Plaintext is not written to ordinary disk in the default mode.
modal.help.body.vault_list.1: The home screen lists every vault in your Upriv root folder. Use the sort menu to order by position, name, state, or last accessed.
modal.help.body.vault_list.2: The view menu switches how vaults are shown: default rows, large cards, compact rows, or block tiles. Sort and view preferences are remembered in system settings.
modal.help.body.vault_list.3: When sorted by position, drag the handle on a row to reorder vaults. Refresh reloads the vault list from disk.
modal.help.body.open_close.1: Unlock asks for the vault password. While unlocking or locking, the row shows Opening or Closing with a time budget. Lock flushes the session into contents/ using the open session — it does not ask for the password again unless you chose Never save. Plaintext-on-disk vaults ask you to confirm before wiping the folder.
modal.help.body.open_close.2: There is no separate Seal step. Lock always closes. Optional idle auto-close locks after inactivity.
modal.help.body.open_close.3: Export is a separate action: copy contents/ into an ordinary .zip, or stream a portable .7z.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.1: Open settings from a vault row gear menu: Preferences (name, storage, idle auto-close, backups, policy), Password, Unlock RAM, and Group (assign this vault). Compression for a portable .7z is chosen when you export.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.2: Save writes config.toml on disk. Some options apply on the next unlock or close. Change password re-wraps keys in contents/; existing backups keep their original password.
modal.help.body.backups.1: When enabled, Upriv can copy contents/ into backups/ on close. Each backup keeps the password from when it was created.
modal.help.body.backups.2: Open Backups from a vault row to list saves (never auto-deleted) and standard backups (rotated per keep-last), download, delete, or create a new vault from a backup (+ icon). Use Save on a standard backup to pin it. Deleting requires typing the vault id to confirm.
modal.help.body.system_settings.1: System settings (⋯ menu) control Language, General (theme, header ⋮), Vault list (toolbar and row buttons), Groups (dragging vaults into groups), logging, and hidden vaults. Language changes UI strings only — vault content is unchanged.
modal.help.body.system_settings.2: To copy a vault to another drive or machine, use Export on that vault’s row. Choose a .zip of encrypted contents (recommended) or a .7z file. There is no bulk download of several vaults at once.
modal.help.body.data_folder.1: Data folder (⋯ menu) chooses where Upriv stores `.upriv/` — settings.toml, vaults/, and logs/. Mount parent (`[workspace].path`) is optional and not auto-created. It is not an individual vault. Use the default location (portable: next to the app; installed: user data) or a custom folder — not both.
modal.help.body.logs.1: View logs (⋯ menu) lists plain-text diagnostic files under `.upriv/logs`. Deleting the active file starts a new one automatically when logging continues.
modal.help.body.logs.2: Open a file to read parsed lines, or select entries to download a zip or delete old logs. Log level in system settings controls how much is written.
modal.help.body.security.1: Session keys live in RAM while a vault is open. In the default mode the password string stays in RAM too so lock does not ask again — only after a successful unlock. A wrong password or a dismissed attempt does not leave the password in that map. Passwords are never stored in settings files, browser storage, or log files.
modal.help.body.security.2: Encrypted directory is recommended: files stay encrypted on disk and you edit via a virtual mount or the in-app file manager. Plaintext-on-disk mode writes readable files while open — simpler but insecure.
modal.help.body.security.3: Access policy controls whether system apps can open the mount (desktop) or in-app files (mobile), and whether copy-out to Desktop, USB, or temp folders is blocked. Blocking copy completely while allowing external editors is hard to enforce.
modal.help.body.recovery.1: If close did not finish cleanly, or leftover plaintext remains from Upriv-plain, the vault enters recovery instead of silently opening.
modal.help.body.recovery.2: Recovery can resume an interrupted close, wipe leftover plaintext, or create a new vault from a backup if the header or index is dead. A single corrupt file does not block the rest of the vault from opening.

modal.vault_root_repair.title: Repair Upriv data folder
modal.vault_root_repair.body: A `.upriv/` folder was found in the default data folder, but it is incomplete or invalid (for example a missing or corrupt `settings.toml`). Choose how to continue.
modal.vault_root_repair.rename_hint: Recommended: rename the broken folder to `.upriv-invalidated-…` so any leftover files (vaults, logs) are kept on disk, then create a fresh `.upriv/`.
modal.vault_root_repair.delete_hint: Delete permanently removes the broken `.upriv/` and creates a new empty one. Vaults and settings inside it cannot be recovered.
modal.vault_root_repair.inspect_hint: Another option: check whether `settings.toml` or other files inside `.upriv/` are wrong or incomplete — fixing them may restore the folder without renaming or deleting.
modal.vault_root_repair.choose_other_hin: Pick a different folder for a new `.upriv/`. The folder is checked first; if it is incomplete, choose rename or delete below before continuing.
modal.app_settings.upriv_root.switch_def: Continuing will create `.upriv/` in the default data folder. `{file}` will be marked inactive (path kept).
Continuing will replace the incomplete `.upriv/` in the default data folder. You can rename it for safekeeping or delete it. `{file}` will be marked inactive (path kept).
modal.app_settings.option.upriv_root.def: Create or use `.upriv/` in the default location. The path pointer is deactivated when using this mode.
Create or use `.upriv/` in your user data folder. You can pick another location with “Choose a custom folder”.
modal.app_settings.option.upriv_root.cus: Store an absolute path in `{file}` in the app home. Rewritten when you change the folder; marked inactive if you switch back to the default data folder.
modal.vault_root_setup.recovery_default_: Create or reopen the default `.upriv/` in the default data folder and use that folder on future launches. Your previous custom path stays in `.upriv-root` as inactive.

modal.settings.option.storage.upriv_plai: + Real files on disk while open (large vaults). Closed: contents/ only. Lock always closes and wipes the folder. − Unprotected while open.
warning.upriv_plain: While open, files are real plaintext on disk — anyone with disk access can read them. Lock encrypts back into contents/ and wipes the folder.
modal.settings.field.seven_zip.compressi: How a portable .7z export is packed. Higher levels make a smaller file but take longer.
modal.settings.option.seven_zip.compress: + Fastest export. − Larger .7z (7-Zip copy mode, no compression).
+ Light compression (7zz -mx=1). − Slightly slower than none.
+ Balanced size and speed (7zz -mx=5). − Default when compressing.
+ Smallest .7z (7zz -mx=9). − Slowest export on large vaults.
modal.settings.option.kdf.32mib_desc: + Lowest RAM here; needs 32 MiB to open. − Weakest offline guessing of these presets.
modal.settings.option.kdf.64mib_desc: + Needs 64 MiB to open. − Easier offline guessing than 128 MiB or the default.
modal.settings.option.kdf.128mib_desc: + Step between 64 MiB and the default; needs 128 MiB to open. − About half the guessing cost of 256 MiB.
modal.settings.option.kdf.256mib_desc: + Default. Needs 256 MiB to open. − Does not stop a weak password.
modal.settings.option.kdf.1gib_desc: + Needs 1 GiB to open; harder parallel guessing than 256 MiB. − Fails if the device cannot allocate 1 GiB.
modal.settings.option.kdf.2gib_desc: + Highest RAM here; needs 2 GiB to open. − Slowest unlock; fails if the device cannot allocate that RAM.
